newsitem.title: USA: Snap-On raises payout, to buy back stock.
newsitem.headline: Snap-On raises payout, to buy back stock.

text.p: Snap-on Inc on Friday said its directors approved a five percent increase in the company's dividend on its common stock and authorized a $100 million share repurchase program.
The quarterly dividend will increase $.01 per share to $0.21 per share, or $0.84 on an annual basis. The increased dividend is payable September 10 to shareholders of record on August 20.
Snap-On, which makes power and hand tools, will make purchases under the buyback program from time to time through the open market and other purchases, the company said in news release.
At current prices, the authorization represents four percent of Snap-On's common shares outstanding.
The repurchases will be made over the next 24 months. Since 1995, Snap-on has repurchased $120 million of its stock through previous authorizations.

Snap-On said it expected to continue to make acquisitions and grow internally. "We have a number of options available for the significant cash generated by our business that will help us meet our stated 10 percent sales and 15 percent average earnings-per-share growth goals," said Robert Cornog, chairman, president and chief executive.
"We have the flexibility to employ that cash in whatever actions will create the greatest shareholder value," he added in a statement.
Snap-on makes tools and equipment for professional technicians, motor service shop owners, specialty repair centers, original equipment manufacturers and industrial tool users.
